summary: The case involved a dispute between the mother and the grandparents of a minor child over the child's surname. The mother, after remarrying, changed the child's surname from Konda to Akella. The grandparents had filed a petition under Section 10 of the Guardian and Wards Act, 1890, seeking guardianship and visitation rights, but did not seek any relief regarding the surname. The High Court directed the restoration of the surname Konda and inclusion of the stepfather's name in records. The Supreme Court held that the mother, as the natural guardian post the father's death, has the right to decide the child's surname and to give the child in adoption. It emphasized that judicial directions altering surnames must be grounded in pleadings, which was absent here. The Court also highlighted the importance of a uniform surname for family identity and child's psychological well-being. The High Court's directions on surname were set aside.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 6, Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956
Section 9(3), Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956
Section 12, Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956
Githa Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India, MANU/SC/0117/1999
Messrs. Trojan & Co. Ltd. v. Rm.N.N. Nagappa Chettiar, AIR 1953 SC 235
Bharat Amratlal Kothari & Anr. v. Dosukhan Samadkhan Sindhi & Ors.
final_judgment: The appeals are allowed. The directions of the High Court regarding the change of the child's surname and inclusion of the stepfather's name are set aside. The mother retains the right to determine the child's surname and to place the child for adoption.
